Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:1: Now that the essence of the blemish itself has been explained in the previous chapters, let us come to explain how many kinds of blemish a person may cause, so that he will fear sinning upon seeing how much evil he brings upon himself, his soul, and all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:2: The first is a blemish to his own body, made in the stamp of the pattern of the supernal worlds; and when one of his limbs is blemished, he becomes one with a defect and the Shechinah does not rest upon him. This is explained in the Tikkunim (130b) - his words: "and in every single limb, which is the candle of every commandment, a person must proclaim the sovereignty of the Holy One, blessed be He, and prepare for Him a pure and clean place to rest there; and therefore a person must clear away from every single limb all thoughts and evil imaginings, the filth that is the kelipot, and must read them by all the commandments that rest upon every single limb in those candles, for every commandment is called a candle, as it is said (Proverbs 6:23) 'for the commandment is a candle' - 'the candle of the Lord is the soul of man' (Proverbs 20:27), and by it one must search all the innermost chambers, and clear from them leaven and chametz, chaff and straw," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:3: And he says further on: "but the Holy One, blessed be He, His sovereignty is in every place, like the soul whose sovereignty is over every single limb - 'the whole earth is full of His glory' - in every place a person calls to Him, He answers him; except that in the place of that limb which is blemished through the sin a person commits, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest in that limb, of which it is said (Leviticus 21:18) 'any who has a defect shall not draw near.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:4: A person's limbs are all arranged according to the order of Creation, and therefore a person is called "a small world," and whoever proclaims the sovereignty of the Holy One, blessed be He, over every single limb is as though he proclaimed His sovereignty over the whole world" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:5: He says further on that there are commandments that depend on the face, and some on the eyes and ears, and he says that YHVH is found in every single limb - He is found in the four colors of hair, the four colors of the eye, the four sections of the ear, the four colors of the face, in voice and speech and reading and utterance, and in the actions of the hands; and in every single limb of the body He, YHVH, is appointed over each and every commandment within it - "mitzvah," by the At-Bash cipher, [becomes] "Mem-Tzadi Yud-Heh Peh-Tzadi Vav-Heh" - so "mitzvah" [corresponds to] YHVH Matzpatz [an alternate rendering of the Name]" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:6: From this a person will see how great a blemish he causes when he blemishes one of his limbs, since all his limbs are stamped with His Name, blessed be He, so he is found to be blemishing the Name; and if he fulfills a mitzvah with that limb, happy is he, for he proclaims YHVH's sovereignty over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:7: Further, they said in the Tikkunim (132a): "happy is he in whom [the Holy One] rests in every single one of his limbs, making a place to rest there and proclaiming His sovereignty in every single limb, so that no limb be empty of Him - for if even one limb lacks the Holy One, blessed be He, resting upon it, on account of that limb he must return to the world through reincarnation until he is completed in his limbs, so that they all be complete in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He - for if even one is lacking, he is not in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He. The Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest in a crooked mouth, for that is a defect; how much more so in crooked speech, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:15) 'that which is crooked cannot be made straight'" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:8: Something of this same blemish is further explained in the Tikkunim (111a) - their words: "certainly, whoever sins in his body - where the deed occurs - and in his soul - where the thought occurs - it is as though he sinned against the One in whose image he was created, as it is said (Genesis 1:27) 'and God created man in His image'" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:9: Further, concerning the blemish caused in a person's own body, Rashbi explains (Acharei 76a), on the verse (Job 16:8) "my leanness rises up against me and testifies to my face" - his words: "Come and see: whoever transgresses the words of the Torah - the Torah ascends and descends and marks the person, leaving signs on his face, so that the upper and lower beings gaze upon him, and they all cast curses upon his head. And we learn that all those 'eyes of the Lord' that go about and roam the world to know the ways of human beings all raise their eyes and gaze upon the face of that person, and see him, and they all open up against him, 'woe, woe' - woe to him in this world, woe to him in the World to Come; remove yourselves from around so-and-so, for a testimony is on his face and a spirit of impurity rests upon him; and all those days that the mark of testimony is found on his face, if he fathers a child, that child draws a spirit from the impure side, and these are the sinners of the generation, brazen of face, whom their Master abandons to their destruction in the World to Come."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:10: We learn: "this righteous one, worthy, who occupies himself with Torah day and night, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws upon him a thread of kindness, marked upon his face, and from that mark the upper and lower beings are in awe; so too, whoever transgresses the words of the Torah, a spirit of impurity is drawn upon him and marked upon his face, and from him the upper and lower beings flee" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:11: Above this it is explained that if one sinned, he should weep and pass tears over his face until the mark passes; and I have heard that it is also good to pass the tears over one's forehead, for iniquities are written on the forehead, along the lines of (Ezekiel 9:4) "and set a mark on the foreheads of the men," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:12: Of this kind are the iniquities written on the hand, as it is written (Job 37:7) "He seals the hand of every man." So too it is explained in the Tikkunim (142b) - his words: "and there are sins of which it is said 'He seals the hand of every man,' and they show them the sealing of their hands" - so far. This is likewise explained in the portion of Lech Lecha (78b), whose words we shall quote below in chapter 12.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:13: The second blemish is a blemish to the soul, in that according to the sin committed, so does it descend, until it lowers it down to his feet. This is explained in the Tikkunim and in Ra'aya Meheimna: in the Tikkunim (132b), "Come and see: there are people who speak with a movement of the eyes, and others with a movement of the hands, and others with a movement of the head, and others with a movement of the body, and others with a movement of the feet - in every place where the soul is, there it makes an extra movement in that place." Rabbi Elazar said to him: father, is the soul not in a known place, in the heart, spreading to all the limbs of the body? He said to him: my son, is it not written of her (Ruth 3:7) 'and she uncovered his feet and lay down'? According to a person's deeds, so it goes out of its place and descends outside its place - like the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Isaiah 50:1) 'and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.' And complete repentance is when one returns her to her place as she was at first. For at the time the soul is in the heart, it is called "Matronita," and when it goes out from the heart, it is not called "Matronita." According to a person's sins, so it descends level by level and limb by limb, until it descends to his feet; and according to his merits, so it ascends until it ascends to its place; and therefore, in every place it descends, it makes an extra movement in that limb more than in the others" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:14: They said, of blessed memory (50a): and concerning the soul in the final exile it is said, "and she uncovered his feet and lay down" - lying down in the dust; woe to the person whose soul has descended beneath his feet, for at that time it is said of it (Amos 5:2) "she has fallen, she shall no longer rise," and there is no ascending and rising for it except by the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:15: Further, a third aspect of the blemish is that according to the blemish a person causes to his soul, so he blemishes the Shechinah, until she descends to the lowest level and "uncovers his feet." This is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim 117b) - his words: "from the side of the wicked - and it is good for him! [ironic] - the Shechinah 'uncovers his feet and lies down' - this is (Proverbs 30:23) 'and a maidservant that supplants her mistress' - the maidservant being the female evil inclination." And he explains afterward the matter of the blemish, saying: but of the Shechinah, the Tree of Life, it is said (Psalms 5:5) "evil shall not dwell with You," and if the maidservant rules, it is in the Throne and below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:16: His words continue: "but because it is said (ibid. 103:19) 'and His kingdom rules over all,' whoever blemishes her place is considered as though he demeans the Matronita, for the demeaning of the Matronita is when one demeans her place, and this is the demeaning of the King's Matronita; how much more so one who removes her from her place and places the maidservant in her place - for in every place he blemishes the Matronita, it is not she who rests there but rather the maidservant, who is blemished, resting in the blemished place. And a person's blemish, from his sins, blemishes all his limbs, until the Matronita finds no place to rest there, and there is no remedy until he restores to her all her limbs" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:17: This is likewise explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Ki Tetzei 277b) - his words: "and this Malchut of Atzilut has, corresponding to her, a Malchut of Beriah, who is queen for the angels of Beriah, and she is the Matronita's handmaiden serving her, and is the image of her mistress, comprised of ten. This one, through Israel's sins, can be profaned among the nations of the world, but of the Malchut of Atzilut of the Holy One, blessed be He, it is said (Isaiah 42:8) 'I am the Lord, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to carven images' - He does not give it to one who profanes Sabbaths and festivals, but only to one who is a son of the King and keeps the Torah in fear and love of his Master, and not in order to receive a reward, but like a son who is obligated to carry out his father's command, of whom it is said (Exodus 20:12) 'honor your father and your mother' - 'your father' is the Holy One, blessed be He, and 'your mother' is the Shechinah; and nonetheless, whoever profanes the King's handmaiden is considered as though he profaned His Matronita" - so far. This point is likewise explained further in the portion of Pinchas (see 226a), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:18: Here he explicitly explains, in this passage, the analogy of the Shechinah, following what he said in the Tikkunim regarding the soul, and the reason for this is that the soul is truly a portion of the Shechinah, as it says (Deuteronomy 32:9) "for the Lord's portion is His people"; and the souls of Israel are of the secret of the [divine] union - "you are children to the Lord your God" (ibid. 14:1) - and there is a union in the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to bring forth a soul on the Sabbath day, and there is a union between them to bring forth a soul on weekdays, these being nefesh from the Throne, ruach from the [world of] Chayah, neshamah from the [world of] Ofan; and concerning the soul of the weekdays is the blemish mentioned in the passage, that she removes it from its place, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:19: Nonetheless, a blemish is sometimes found even in one who has a soul of Atzilut, as is said in the Tikkunim (99b) regarding the sin of Adam, the first man, that in the very place from which his soul was taken, there he sinned. The reason is that as the souls, which are the branches below, act, so they arouse the roots above. And although sin does not come through one who has a soul of Atzilut, nevertheless the withdrawal of the soul from him is what is called a blemish; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (124a): a person commits sins - according to that person, so his sin ascends to the place from which his soul was hewn, and that sin does not move from there until payment is exacted from that person; and if a person's soul is on the path of Atzilut, if he sins, his sin reaches all the way to the sefirot, and the punishment is very great according to his level.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:20: Rabbi Elazar said: father, is sin then dependent upon the person whose soul is from that place, and does he really have [such power]? Behold, it is written (Proverbs 12:21) "no harm shall befall the righteous." He said to him: yes, this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 59:2) "but your iniquities have separated between you and your God" - separated whom? Rather, that this soul of Atzilut ascends from him and separates from him, and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 1:9) "and God said, let the waters under the heaven be gathered," etc. - his soul ascended from him and a dry body remained. What body is this? This is the soul of the Throne of Glory, which remained dry, because the soul of the path of Atzilut ascended from it - for this [lower] soul is a body for the supernal soul, and if it wishes to return to that soul, it has no permission to return to it until that sin is removed from it, and the secret of the matter is (Malachi 3:7) "return to Me and I will return to you"" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:21: This is an introduction to all the blemishes that will be explained regarding the removal of the Mother from over the children, etc. - all of this follows this pattern, and it is possible to distinguish between the individual and the many; and there is a hint of proof in the Zohar (Vayikra 15b), which says that when the sins of the world increase, the Ancient Holy One withdraws and does not gaze face to face, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:22: Further, concerning the blemish of the Shechinah, it is explained in the Tikkunim (58b) - their words: "and when the central pillar distances itself from her, it is judgment, and of this it is written (Psalms 75:8) 'for God is judge; He puts down one and lifts up another' - 'He puts down one' - one who causes the Shechinah to be lowered from her place; 'and lifts up another' - one who causes her to be raised to her place; for the sins of Israel lower her below, and their merits raise her to her place - happy is he who performs merits to raise her to her place" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:23: Further, a person's blemish upon the Shechinah and upon the other levels below her is explained in what is explained in the Tikkunim (65a) - it says there that souls, angels, and holy Chayot are engraved in the Shechinah, and engraved in her is what is said (Ezekiel 1:10) "and their faces had the likeness of a man's face." Rabbi Shimon rose and said: elder, elder, but the Shechinah is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He - how are images of the lower beings, which are not her true reality, engraved in her? He said to him: it is like a king who sits in his palace, and several people enter to see him - some gaze at his garments, some at his body, and some gaze at his deeds; and certainly it is by his deeds that one recognizes what the king is, for his garments change many times - the garment he wears in the morning he does not wear in the evening, and the garment he wears one day he does not wear the next day; and so too every day and month and year and Sabbath and festival, his garments change.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:24: In this manner, the Shechinah has many garments, from which the Holy One, blessed be He, created thrones, angels, Chayot, seraphim, heaven and earth and all that He created within them, and all the created beings He created from these garments are marked and engraved by Him in her garments, so that from her all creatures may be gazed upon, to have mercy on them; and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 9:16) "and I will look upon it, to remember the everlasting covenant" - and I will look upon it in these garments, which shine within all creatures - Israel illuminates them through good deeds, and because of them the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them; but if they do evil deeds, she clothes herself in other, black garments, in which all those masters of judgment, called Lilith, who judge the world, are marked; and at that time she says (Song of Songs 1:6) "do not look at me, for I am swarthy," etc.; and therefore these, from the side of the garments, are engraved in her, supernal, etc." - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:25: We find, then, that in these garments all existing things are depicted, and they are the roots within her from which the reality of all the lower worlds emerge; and when the roots within her shine through the commandments that Israel fulfills below, there is mercy and goodness in the world, and when Israel does not perfect their deeds, all her garments draw from the side of judgment and darkness, and then she says "do not look at me, for I am swarthy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:26: With this we understand what they say in the Tikkunim, printed in the portion of Bereishit (Zohar 23b): whoever sins against the Shechinah is as though he stripped the Shechinah of her garments - and this is the punishment for Adam - and whoever fulfills a commandment of the Torah is as though he clothed the Shechinah in her garments - so far. The meaning is that through sin one strips her of her beautiful, shining garments and clothes her in garments of blackness, as explained in this passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:27: He says further there (Hashmatot 252b), that the Shechinah is the "pupil of the eye" [bat ayin], dark, with a light shining within it from inside, and concerning this David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 27:1) "the Lord is my light" - the light of the Yud, which is the pupil of the eye. And he says: she has two colors, light within and darkness without, so that she may rule over all the kelipot through them - this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 103:19) "and His kingdom rules over all" - in the garment of light she rules over all those of whom it is said (Exodus 10:23) "and all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings," and in the black garment she rules over all the wicked, of whom it is said (I Samuel 2:9) "and the wicked shall be silenced in darkness" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:28: From the root of the soul rooted in her, man either perfects or blemishes, as it says, "souls are engraved in her"; and therefore, when he blemishes below, he darkens the root of his soul, rooted in the Shechinah, and then, through his sin, he withholds the good from himself, since she has no "face" [standing] with which to ask for a flow on his behalf.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:29: Along these lines, the blemish a person causes wherever he blemishes is understood through the root of the soul rooted in all places, for wherever the soul passes, its form remains depicted there. My teacher, peace be upon him, explains that through the root of the soul depicted there, a person arouses "female waters" within the Shechinah when he says (Psalms 25:1) "to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul," as is explained in the Zohar (Vayakhel 202b; Bemidbar 120b); and if his soul is blemished, without doubt it will not be included in the [divine] union and will arouse nothing, for since the branch is blemished, the root is also blemished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:30: Along these lines, Rashbi explains (Terumah 129a) that Yehudiam is appointed over the images of the righteous, and he says there that whoever brings the wicked back in repentance arouses his soul above in union when he says "to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul," and Yehudiam carries his image upward, and they bless it with several blessings - his words: "at that hour a certain appointee is summoned, who is the treasurer over the images of the righteous, in the secret of the service of the letters, called by the secret name Yehudiam, in the crown of the service of the Holy Name; and the Holy One, blessed be He, hints, and that appointee brings the image of that person who saves the souls of the wicked, and it stands before the King and the Matronita, and I call heaven and earth to witness that at that hour that image is delivered to him - for there is no righteous person in this world whose image is not engraved above, beneath the hand of that appointee, and seventy keys to all his Master's treasuries are delivered into his hand; then the King blesses that image with all the blessings with which He blessed Abraham, so does He do for the one who saves the souls of the wicked," etc. - so far. They elaborate further there on the merit of one who brings the wicked back in repentance, which is not relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:31: Further, it is explained in the portion of Vayeshev (Zohar 191a) that all images are depicted in the Shechinah, and it says there that when a person is complete in his image - meaning in the countenance of the soul, called "Adam," that he has not sinned - all creatures fear him, as it is written (Genesis 9:2) "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth," etc. And it says: this is so when the soul is within him - meaning, when he has not blemished his body such that the soul departs from him; but once there is a blemish in the body, the soul departs from him and he becomes like an animal, as it says (Psalms 49:13) "but man, in glory, does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish" - and man's "glory" is his soul, and one who sins and causes the soul not to abide within him is likened to the beasts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:32: He raises a difficulty: but of Daniel it is written (Daniel 6:23) "my God has sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me" - implying that it was the angel that shut them, not his image. He resolves this by saying that the angel itself is his image, meaning the image engraved in the Shechinah, called an "angel" - his words: "he said to him: therefore he was not harmed, for that righteous person's image is truly an angel who shuts their mouths and binds them to guard him so that they should not harm him; and therefore, 'my God sent His angel' - the one in whom all the images of the world are engraved, and he strengthened his image within it, so that they could not have power over me, and shut their mouths; and therefore 'He sent His angel,' certainly. And this angel, in whom all images are engraved, of whom it is written (Psalms 110:6) 'He shall judge among the nations, filling [them] with corpses [or: filling the bodies]' - he does not change before all the images of the world; and therefore a person must guard his ways and paths so that he not sin before his Master, and thereby be established in the image of Adam" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:33: Now that we know that all the images of the righteous are there, without doubt if the image below is blemished, the image above will not be seen before the whole retinue above, since "any who has a defect shall not draw near." When a person contemplates this matter, he will feel shame and be humbled by his sins, for every single sin is an affliction and a defect in his soul, and his image above becomes distanced from holiness, as Scripture says of the leper (Leviticus 13:45-46) "and the leper in whom is the plague, his clothes shall be torn... and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, unclean, unclean," and it says "he shall dwell alone, outside the camp shall be his dwelling." The blemish in the soul and its distancing from supernal holiness is what causes the body below likewise to be distanced from the camp of Israel; and if a person repents to purify his defects by accepting sufferings upon himself, he thereby purifies himself of his leprosy; but if not, that leprosy remains fixed in his soul, and in this world and the World to Come he is distanced from the whole retinue above until he is purified. Therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 22b) that David the king, peace be upon him, was afflicted with leprosy for six months, since it is better that the blemish rise up in the body in this world than that the defect and leprosy remain in the soul, to be punished in Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:34: This introduction - that all souls are rooted there - is further explained in the Tikkunim (65b), and likewise regarding ruach and neshamah - his words: "'set me as a seal' - this is the soul, whose mark is engraved above, as they have established regarding Jacob, whose image is engraved on the Throne of Glory; for all souls that are hewn from there, their engraving is engraved above and their mark is below, and that engraving above is the seal, and the mark below is the mark of the seal. And as soon as the mark of the soul's engraving is above and its mark is below, it is said of it (Genesis 28:12) 'and behold, angels of God ascending and descending on it' - they ascend above and gaze at the image of the soul that shines in that engraving, and are awed by it; they descend below and gaze at the mark of that image below, and see that it has not changed from the image above, and they fear it" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:35: We find, then, that when the lower image is intact, without blemish, the angels fear it, because its image has not changed from the supernal image depicted on the Throne; and perhaps this is what is meant by (Genesis 9:2) "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and every bird of the heavens." "The beasts of the earth" are the angels of the Shechinah, and "the birds of the heavens" are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, along the lines explained in the Tikkunim (2b): "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" (Ecclesiastes 10:20) - referring to Metatron.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:36: In the Zohar (Noach 71a), "the beasts of the earth," etc., is explained according to its plain sense, and it says that when the form of man is without sin, all creatures fear him, and if not, God forbid, they all rule over him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:37: In the Pekudin of Rabbi Shimon (Zohar, Naso 123b), this verse is explained in another way - his words: "and because everything was created in this image, concerning all of Israel, who is righteous, it is said, 'and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and every bird of the heavens,' etc. This speaks of human beings who are compared to wild animals, cattle, birds, and fish of the sea - there is a person whose zodiacal sign is an ox, and one whose sign is a lion, and one whose sign is an eagle, and one whose sign is a man - and why do all these tremble before this image, since they were created from there? Rather, it is because the Name YHVH rests upon it, and the secret of the matter is (Deuteronomy 28:10) 'and all the peoples of the earth shall see,' etc.; and whoever blemishes his deeds, his image is blemished, and the Name YHVH does not rest in a blemished place" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:38: There, above this matter, it says that according to a person's deeds, so does he merit the image of holiness or its opposite - his words: "just as there is a good image over the righteous, guiding him in all good deeds to merit him for the World to Come, so there is an evil image over the head of the wicked, guiding them in evil deeds that inherit Gehinnom; and therefore there is 'vanity' [hevel] and there is 'vanity' - there is a good 'breath' [hevel], of which it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3) 'for by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord man lives,' and there is an evil 'vanity,' of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:14) 'this too is vanity and a vexation of spirit.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 9:39: Come and see: through a person's deeds, the countenance [partzuf] that is upon him is recognized, and in the countenance of his face, as it is said (Isaiah 3:9) "the very look on their faces testifies against them" - in the image, the countenance of the Chayah that rests upon him is recognized, whether it is a lion or an ox or an eagle or a man - from the Chariot of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, or from the Chariot of the angel, the Prince of the Countenance, or from the evil Chariot of Samael, or from the Chariot of the four elements of the world, which have neither good inclination nor evil inclination but are like the beasts of the world; and therefore there are many kinds of "vanity" among human beings, each according to its kind, and the secret of the matter is (Genesis 1:24) "let the earth bring forth the living soul after its kind"; and therefore, in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him" - so far. And what he says, "there is a good 'breath,' of which it is said, 'for by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord,'" etc., refers to the Shechinah, as is also explained there at the beginning of the passage, see there.
